name: Debug Cacheability Headers Split
description: Detects when Drupal core's debug cacheability headers exceed a server's per-header size limit and splits the value across multiple numbered headers.
project_description: Most web servers enforce a maximum size per HTTP header; a common limit is 8KB. When Drupal core's http.response.debug_cacheability_headers setting is enabled, the X-Drupal-Cache-Tags and X-Drupal-Cache-Contexts headers are emitted, and on complex pages the list of cache tags/contexts can be large enough that a single header exceeds the server limit, producing errors such as a white screen of death or a 502 Bad Gateway. This module registers a response event subscriber that inspects those two headers on cacheable main responses and, when a header's byte length exceeds a configurable size limit, word-wraps the value into chunks and re-emits it across numbered headers (e.g. X-Drupal-Cache-Tags, X-Drupal-Cache-Tags-1, X-Drupal-Cache-Tags-2). Two thresholds are configurable at /admin/config/development/settings/cacheability or via settings.local.php: the size limit above which a header is split (default 8192, minimum 1024) and the maximum chunk size for each split header (default 8000, minimum 512). The module is a development/debugging aid and takes no action unless core's debug cacheability headers are enabled.
